body.statement:
For any fixed \(\bar\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), with \(p,k,L,B,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}\) fixed, for every \(n\ge1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{\substack{\|\beta\|_2\le B,\;\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\\
 \textnormal{admissible conditional-noise laws}}}
 \left|
 \frac{R_n(\beta,\sigma,\bar\varepsilon)}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star/n}-1
 \right|\\
 &\qquad\le
 \frac{\mu^\star-1}{(1-\bar\varepsilon)n}
 +2q\left(1+\mu^\star+
 \frac{nB^2}{\sigma_{\min}^2\Phi^\star}\right)
 \exp\!\left(-\frac{n\bar\varepsilon^2}{3\mu^\star}\right)
 =O(n^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, the displayed supremum converges to zero. This is a uniform fixed-dimensional oracle-risk expansion for the specified estimator at \(d^\star\); it is not a finite-\(n\) minimax-optimality statement over dosage designs.
body.justification: This gives a finite-sample, uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) relative-risk expansion for the fixed-threshold known-information estimator at the exact population-optimal dosage.
body.gap: PFED does not provide an all-order shared-supply oracle constant, and the generic concentration references do not derive the mean-cancelled second-order remainder with this exact leverage and fallback term.
body.consumer: An independent-delivery interaction screen can use a fixed conditioning threshold and read off a uniform finite-sample error bound around the population oracle risk, without interpreting it as finite-sample design minimaxity.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\bar\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\) according to \(\textnormal{def:oracle-threshold}\). By the fixed-dimension assumption, \(q\), \(\mu^\star\), \(\Phi^\star\), \(B\), and \(\sigma_{\min}\) are constants as \(n\to\infty\). The exact-leverage and trace results used inside \(\textnormal{thm:risk-sandwich}\) ensure \(1<\mu^\star<\infty\) and \(0<\Phi^\star<\infty\). Hence the normalizing factor \(\sigma^2\Phi^\star/n\) is positive uniformly over \(\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\).

For an admissible coefficient, noise scale, and conditional-noise law, define in this proof
\[
 \rho_n(\beta,\sigma)
 =\frac{R_n(\beta,\sigma,\bar\varepsilon)}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star/n}.
\]
The second-order conclusion of \(\textnormal{thm:risk-sandwich}\), together with \(\|\beta\|_2\le B\) and \(\sigma^2\ge\sigma_{\min}^2\), gives simultaneously over the entire displayed class
\[
 \left|\rho_n(\beta,\sigma)-1\right|
 \le
 \frac{\mu^\star-1}{(1-\bar\varepsilon)n}
 +2q\left(1+\mu^\star+
 \frac{nB^2}{\sigma_{\min}^2\Phi^\star}\right)
 \exp\!\left(-\frac{n\bar\varepsilon^2}{3\mu^\star}\right). \tag{1}
\]
The right-hand side is deterministic and independent of \(\beta\), \(\sigma\), and the particular admissible conditional-noise law. Taking the supremum therefore preserves inequality \((1)\).

Set \(c=\bar\varepsilon^2/(3\mu^\star)>0\). Elementary differentiation shows that \(x^me^{-cx}\) is bounded on \([1,\infty)\) for each fixed integer \(m\ge0\): its only positive critical point is \(x=m/c\), and it tends to zero at infinity. In particular, both \(ne^{-cn}\) and \(n^2e^{-cn}\) are bounded. Multiplying the exponential term in \((1)\) by \(n\) consequently leaves a bounded sequence. The first term is exactly a fixed constant times \(n^{-1}\), so the entire right-hand side is \(O(n^{-1})\) and converges to zero.

This proves the explicit uniform oracle-risk expansion for the known-information, fixed-threshold estimator under independent product-Bernoulli delivery. It concerns the estimator evaluated at \(d^\star\) only. No step supplies a lower bound over competing finite-sample dosage designs, so no finite-\(n\) dosage-minimax claim is made.
